site.title: Exit Chat Control · Become Ungovernable
site.description: Field guide to escape Chat Control and protect your privacy: encrypted messaging, e-mail, VPN, passwords, Linux, GrapheneOS. Free, open source, no tracking.

hero.lede: Chat Control wants to scan your private messages. Here is how to take back control of your conversations, your data and your tools, step by step, from beginner to whistleblower.

status.label: Status · October 2026
status.headline: Chat Control 1.0 is back in force, until 3 April 2028.
status.body: After the motion to reject failed in the European Parliament on 9 July (314 votes in favour, 361 needed), the Council gave the text final approval on 23 July 2026. Providers may again scan private communications "voluntarily", except end-to-end encrypted communications, which an amendment excludes. In parallel, Chat Control 2.0 (CSAR), the permanent regulation, is still under negotiation: the 29 September trilogue ended without agreement.
status.cta: This guide assumes a harsher version may follow: the tools presented here stay protective in that scenario.

noscript.notice: JavaScript is disabled: good instinct. The entire guide works without it: only the theme toggle, filters and checklist need scripts.

footer.proofline: Zero trackers, zero cookies, zero external requests. Everything (fonts, icons, styles) is embedded. Verify it: open the network inspector, reload. Nothing leaves for a third party.
footer.disclaimer: This guide is an information document on privacy protection and the defence of encryption. It advises no illegal activity. Always check the legislative news: the situation moves fast.

manifesto.label: Manifesto
manifesto.p1: Changing tools is an act of individual responsibility, one that belongs to each of us: it is how you refuse an illegitimate mass surveillance.
manifesto.p2: Encrypting is protecting your private life. Self-hosting is pulling yourself out of Big Tech's surveillance. Taking back control of your tools is becoming ungovernable and sovereign.
manifesto.p3: The fight is political. Support the organisations opposing it, like the {link} initiative, and write to your representatives. That is what almost brought Chat Control down.
manifesto.p4: But since the solution will probably come neither from the ballot box nor from the European Parliament, it falls to each of us to win our freedom and protect our privacy with every tool the Internet offers.
